## Upstream changes 0.40.1 -> 0.40.2

**Verdict:** SAFE TO APPLY — the notes describe a one-time background model upgrade and minor CLI fixes; the image configuration itself is unchanged in every field that affects deployment.

### Breaking changes
- none found in the notes. The model-upgrade process is described as transparent to the user ("Models downloaded with earlier versions of Ollama are upgraded in the background the first time you run them"), not a compatibility break.

### Variables
- none

### Data and dependencies
- Disk usage will grow temporarily: "To make downgrading safe, Ollama keeps the original copy as a backup, so upgraded models are temporarily kept on disk." This applies per-model, the first time each existing model is run after the upgrade. The `ollama-data` volume should have headroom for roughly double the size of whichever models get re-run.
- Downgrade path is time-limited: "If you later downgrade to a version older than 0.40, you'll need to re-pull those models." This only matters if a rollback below 0.40 is later attempted; it does not block this 0.40.1 → 0.40.2 move.
- No companion service (database, cache, search engine) version is named anywhere in these notes, so the no-SAFE-TO-APPLY rule for an unpinned dependency does not apply here.

### Before applying
- None required before applying. Optionally, after the upgrade, once models have been re-run and upgraded, the operator can reclaim disk space with the cleanup command given in the notes (requires `jq` inside or alongside the container):
  ```
  curl -s localhost:11434/api/tags | jq -r '.models[].name' | while read -r m; do
    curl -s localhost:11434/api/show -d "{\"model\":\"$m\"}" | jq -r \
      'select(any(.manifests[]?; .runner == "llamacpp")) | .manifests[] | select(.runner == "ggml") | .digest'
  done | sort -u | xargs -n1 ollama rm
  ```
  Do not run this if a downgrade below 0.40 is still possible, since it deletes the backups needed for that path.

### Notes read
- v0.40.2 (2026-10-08) — the version being moved to
- v0.40.1 (2026-10-07) — the baseline currently running, read only to confirm no carried-over requirement applies
